$comment: The snapnedit embed wire protocol, machine-readable. Checked against protocol.ts/types.ts by packages/embed/test/protocol-json.test.ts — every method, event and error code must appear here, so a wrapper generated from this file cannot fall behind the TypeScript loader. Human-readable companion: docs/embed-protocol.md.
name: snapnedit-embed

envelope.note: Every message is a JSON object carrying `snapnedit: 1` (the protocol version) and a `type`. Over postMessage it crosses as a structured-cloned object; over the native transport as the same object JSON.stringify'd to a string. Structured-clone-only values (Blob) are re-encoded for the native transport — see `native.blobEncoding`.

hostToFrame.note: Accepted exactly once, and only from the origin the frame was opened for. On the native transport the frame synthesizes its own init from the URL query, so a shell never needs to send one.
`id` is opaque and echoed back on the matching `result`.
Answers a `token-expiring` event with a freshly minted embed token.

frameToHost.note: The frame is listening. On the native transport it is buffered until an outbound channel exists.

loadImage.note: A string must be an absolute https:, blob: or data: URL, never on the frame's own origin. Native shells pass a data: URL or an https: URL — blob: cannot cross the process boundary.

export.result: { blob: Blob, width: number, height: number }
export.note: Over the native transport a Blob cannot be JSON-serialized, so the `blob` value arrives as `{ dataUrl, mime, bytes }` in its place. See `native.blobEncoding`.

exportTo.note: Renders exactly what `export` renders and PUTs the bytes to a presigned url or a saved storage destination. JSON-safe on both transports.

export.note: Fired by the frame's own Export menu. Over the native transport the `blob` value arrives as `{ dataUrl, mime, bytes }` — see `native.blobEncoding`.

transport.note: Anything else keeps the frame on the postMessage transport.

origin.note: The shell's self-asserted app id, lower-cased by the api. Must be listed in the publishable key's allowed origins (dashboard → API keys). Sent to POST /embed/sessions as `hostOrigin` and carried in the issued token's `origin` claim.

key.note: A pk_ publishable key. Exactly one of `key` or `token` is required.

token.note: A host-server-minted embed token (POST /embed/tokens). Skips the allowlist check.

locale.note: UI locale, e.g. `en`. Unknown values fall back to the default.

buffering.note: Outbound messages produced before any channel exists are buffered and flushed the moment one is detected — detection is retried on every send and on the first receive() call.

blobEncoding.note: The ONE difference between the two transports, and it is mechanical rather than protocol-level: JSON has no Blob, so before serializing an envelope the frame walks it and replaces every Blob value, wherever it sits, with a JSON object of the same key. Nothing else about the envelope changes. Affects `export`'s result and the `export` event; every other method is already JSON-safe.

payloadLimits.note: Both directions cross the JS/native boundary as one string. Keep inbound data: URLs under a few MB (evaluateJavaScript/ExecuteScriptAsync copy the whole string); for anything larger hand the frame an https: URL instead, or upload with exportTo rather than reading a data: URL back out.

errorEnvelope.note: A receive() payload that is not parseable JSON, or is not a protocol message, is answered with an `error` event rather than being ignored — a shell with a serialization bug hears about it.

data.message: SnapneditNativeBridge.receive: payload is not valid JSON
